data.long_meaning: Originally derived from the Greek name 'Melanios', meaning 'black'. In the Bible, Melchizedek is a king of Salem and a priest, who offers a sacrifice to God. Melanion is a character in Greek mythology, a shepherd who was transformed into a stag and hunted by his own hounds. The name Mel carries the meaning “Black” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Mel usually hope their child will grow to embody black and live with faith, good character and purpose.
